genres.notes: Answers "Can you teach me to…?" - reader is *studying* by *doing*. Choose over how-to when the reader is a novice and the aim is learning, not a specific task. A tutorial is not the place for explanation - link an Explanation instead.
Answers "How do I…?" - reader is *working* by *doing*. A recipe, not a lesson; it assumes competence and solves one real-world problem.
Answers "What is…?" - reader is *working* by *thinking*, consulting facts rather than performing steps - describe and only describe, no teaching or opinion.
Answers "Why…?" / "Can you tell me about…?" - reader is *studying* by *thinking*. The mode you can read away from the keyboard, and the place for alternatives, counter-examples, and context.

slots.name: id
slots.description: The concept's stable IRI. By convention it is the bundle base IRI joined with the Concept ID (the file path within the bundle, minus the `.md` suffix). Becomes the JSON-LD @id / RDF subject.

slots.name: type
slots.description: The concept's type - OKF's single required field. SHOULD name a LOKF class (e.g. Metric, Dataset, Table, Playbook, GlossaryTerm).

slots.name: title
slots.description: Human-readable display name.

slots.name: description
slots.description: A single-sentence summary of the concept.

slots.name: resource
slots.description: A URI that uniquely identifies the underlying real-world asset the concept describes (a table console URL, an API base URL, etc.). Absent for purely abstract concepts.

slots.name: tags
slots.description: Short cross-cutting keywords for categorization.

slots.name: timestamp
slots.description: ISO 8601 datetime of the last meaningful change.

slots.name: created
slots.description: ISO 8601 datetime the concept was created.

slots.name: version
slots.description: A version string for the concept's content.

slots.name: license
slots.description: The license under which the concept or bundle is offered.

slots.name: author
slots.description: The agent(s) responsible for authoring the concept.

slots.name: publisher
slots.description: The agent responsible for making the bundle available.

slots.name: body
slots.description: The markdown body of the concept document (everything after the frontmatter). Mapped to schema:text; carried as a field only in the JSON-LD / JSON serialization, not duplicated in the frontmatter.

slots.name: citations
slots.description: External sources supporting claims in the body.

slots.name: concepts
slots.description: The concepts contained in a bundle.

slots.name: relations
slots.description: Typed relationships whose predicate is not covered by a named relation slot. Each entry is a reified Relation (predicate + target).

slots.name: isPartOf
slots.description: The target concept that this concept is a part of.

slots.name: hasPart
slots.description: A concept that is a part of this concept.

slots.name: references
slots.description: A concept or resource this concept refers to.

slots.name: dependsOn
slots.description: A concept this concept depends on.

slots.name: derivedFrom
slots.description: An entity this concept was derived from (provenance).

slots.name: about
slots.description: The subject matter this concept is about.

slots.name: sameAs
slots.description: An IRI asserting this concept is the same entity as another.

slots.name: relatedTo
slots.description: A generic association to another concept.

slots.name: definedBy
slots.description: A resource that formally defines this concept.

slots.name: source
slots.description: A resource from which this concept is derived or sourced.

slots.name: genre
slots.description: The Diátaxis documentation mode of the concept's markdown body (tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation). An optional facet orthogonal to `type`: `type` says what the concept is *about*, `genre` says how its prose *serves the reader*.

slots.name: predicate
slots.description: The relationship type. SHOULD be drawn from the RelationType vocabulary.

slots.name: target
slots.description: The IRI (or Concept ID) of the relationship's object.

slots.name: relation_label
slots.description: An optional human-readable label for the relationship.

slots.name: distribution
slots.description: Accessible forms of the dataset.

slots.name: fields
slots.description: The columns / properties that make up a dataset's schema.

slots.name: name
slots.description: A name.

slots.name: email
slots.description: Contact email address.

slots.name: datatype
slots.description: The data type of a field.

slots.name: unit
slots.description: The unit of measurement (e.g. USD, seconds, count).

slots.name: is_key
slots.description: Whether the field is (part of) the primary key.

slots.name: constraints
slots.description: Free-text or expression describing constraints on a field.

slots.name: access_url
slots.description: A URL that gives access to a distribution.

slots.name: media_type
slots.description: The media (MIME) type of a distribution.

slots.name: formula
slots.description: The calculation or definition expression for a metric.

slots.name: measures
slots.description: What the metric measures (a concept IRI or description).

slots.name: endpoint
slots.description: The base URL or invocation endpoint of a service.

slots.name: http_method
slots.description: The HTTP method used to invoke the service, if applicable.

slots.name: documentation
slots.description: A link to the service's documentation.

slots.name: definition
slots.description: The formal definition of a term.

slots.name: abbreviation
slots.description: A short form or acronym for a term.

slots.name: roleName
slots.description: The name/title of the role held (e.g. a job title).

slots.name: startDate
slots.description: The date the role began (ISO 8601 date or year).

slots.name: endDate
slots.description: The date the role ended; omit for a role still held.

slots.name: memberOf
slots.description: The organization within which the role is held.

slots.name: holder
slots.description: The agent (typically a Person) who holds the role.

slots.name: url
slots.description: A URL.

slots.name: lokf_version
slots.description: The LOKF version the bundle targets (e.g. "0.2").

slots.name: okf_version
slots.description: The OKF version the bundle remains compatible with (e.g. "0.2").

slots.name: base_iri
slots.description: The base IRI against which Concept IDs are resolved to produce each concept's stable `id`. An identifier namespace, not a hyperlink: it need not resolve to a live page (a 404 is valid), so it is only required to be a well-formed absolute IRI with an authority. A resolvable "Cool URI" is the ideal, not a requirement.

slots.name: context
slots.description: The URL of the JSON-LD @context to attach to this bundle's concepts to interpret their frontmatter as Linked Data.

slots.name: sources
slots.description: The materials this concept derives from, each carrying objective credibility signals. Markdown footnotes join to entries via `sources[].id`. Supersedes `citations` and the body `# Citations` convention.

slots.name: usage_window
slots.description: The `{ from, to }` date range framing every `usage_count`. Attached both to Concept (the shared window, sibling of `sources`) and to Source (a per-entry override).

slots.name: from
slots.description: Start date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD) of a usage window.

slots.name: to
slots.description: End date (inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD) of a usage window.

slots.name: usage_count
slots.description: How often the source's resource was exercised (views, executions, reads) over the governing usage_window. An adoption/liveness signal read as order-of-magnitude and trend, not a score.

slots.name: last_modified
slots.description: When the SOURCE itself last changed (YYYY-MM-DD). A recency signal about the source, distinct from `generated.at`, which records when this concept's content was produced. Same predicate as the deprecated `timestamp`, on a different subject node (source vs concept).

slots.name: generated
slots.description: How and when the current content was produced: `by` (REQUIRED actor) and `at` (ISO 8601 datetime). Supersedes the v0.1 `timestamp` field; consumers MAY fall back to `timestamp` when `generated` is absent.

slots.name: verified
slots.description: Verification events confirming the content against its sources or resource. Independent of `generated`: who wrote a concept need not be who confirmed it. Trust tiers derive from the actors: absent = unverified; only non-human actors = machine-confirmed; any `human:<id>` actor = human-reviewed.

slots.name: by
slots.description: The actor that performed the event, as a plain OKF §7 actor string (`<producer>/<version>`, `human:<id>`, `process:<id>`) — a literal, never an IRI. Trust tiers derive from the `human:` prefix via string inspection (SPARQL STRSTARTS).

slots.name: at
slots.description: ISO 8601 datetime at which the event completed.

slots.name: status
slots.description: Lifecycle status of the concept: draft | stable | deprecated. Absent means stable. Advisory, never access control.

slots.name: stale_after
slots.description: Absolute date (YYYY-MM-DD) on or after which the concept is stale (stale when today >= stale_after).

slots.name: runtime
slots.description: REQUIRED on an Attested Computation. How to run the computation (bigquery | postgres | dbt | python | Looker | ...); defines what `parameters` mean and how the executor and attester interpret the contract.

slots.name: parameters
slots.description: The typed, named holes the agent may fill — the ONLY surface the agent may bind. Binding semantics follow `runtime`.

slots.name: required
slots.description: Whether a value for the parameter must be supplied.

slots.name: computation
slots.description: Optional path to a file holding the computation; absent means the body's `# Computation` fenced block IS the computation. Minted in lokf: schema:contentUrl is the nearest real property but is scoped to MediaObject bytes.

slots.name: executor
slots.description: How the computation is run and what evidence a run must return.

slots.name: receipt
slots.description: The field names a run must return (e.g. job_id, executed_sql, result) — the evidence the attester inspects. Receipts themselves are runtime artifacts, never stored in the bundle. Minted in lokf: no established vocabulary describes a receipt-shape declaration.

slots.name: attester
slots.description: The deterministic, non-LLM verdict check over a receipt.
